items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Proposition: for a morphism f : X -> T of algebraic spaces over a scheme S with T representable, f locally quasi-finite and f separated, the algebraic space X is representable (source lines 10806-10817). The proof is a multi-stage reduction that cannot be replaced by a citation: it reduces to an affine base by a Zariski covering, then to the case where an affine U maps surjectively etale onto X, forms the etale equivalence relation R = U x_X U presenting X as U/R, checks the seven hypotheses of the More on Groupoids quasi-finiteness lemma for the groupoid (U, R, s, t, c) over T at a chosen pair of points (u, p), and applies it to obtain an etale neighbourhood (T', p') and a disjoint union decomposition whose affine quotient U'/R' is an open subspace of X_{T'}. The closing step turns this local affine neighbourhood into a global representability statement via the neighbourhood-scheme lemma.
